ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence on all politically exposed persons (PEPs), including foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, and international organization PEPs, their family members and close associates, under Part 2 Subpart 1 of the AML/CFT Act 2009 and the Financial Markets Authority AML/CFT Supervisors Handbook. The screening must be run on a continuous pre-incorporation and post-incorporation basis against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; the New Zealand consolidated sanctions list administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade; the United States Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list; the United Kingdom HM Treasury consolidated list; the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list; Interpol notices; New Zealand Police warnings; and the FATF high-risk and monitored jurisdiction list. All directors, shareholders, UBOs, senior managers, and any material intermediaries must be screened within 24 hours before the registration filing and the results archived in the AML/CFT compliance file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office Company Register (https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz) operated by the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), integrated with the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) portal (https://www.nzbn.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All proposed company names must be submitted in the Latin (Roman) script. If the proposed name contains diacritical marks, including Maori macrons, or non-Latin characters, an ASCII-equivalent transliteration or a certified transliteration must be filed with the Registrar. The name must not be identical or practically identical to any name already registered or reserved in New Zealand. The legal suffix Limited (or the Maori equivalent Tapui) or the abbreviation Ltd is mandatory for an International Company with limited liability. A name will be refused if it is offensive, contrary to law, likely to mislead, or implies a connection with the Crown, a government department, a local authority, a foreign sovereign state, or an international body.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal by the Registrar of Companies under sections 22 and 23 of the Companies Act 1993, the applicant may file a written application for reconsideration with the Registrar through the Companies Office portal within 20 working days of the refusal, stating the legal and factual grounds and attaching any supporting evidence, including evidence of consent from any relevant minister, regulator, or professional body. The Registrar will issue a reconsideration decision within a further 20 working days. If the refusal is maintained, the applicant may seek judicial review of the Registrar's decision in the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016. An expiring name reservation may be preserved by filing a fresh application for the same name before expiry and paying the applicable reapplication fee; availability of the name will be subject to the register status at that time.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address maintained by a licensed registered agent satisfies the registered office requirement in section 189 of the Companies Act 1993, provided that a physical street address in New Zealand is maintained for service of documents and statutory records. However, for a retail securities brokerage licensed under Part 6 of the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, the Financial Markets Authority will require a genuine place of business in New Zealand, with operational staff, supervisory oversight, client money record-keeping infrastructure, and AML/CFT systems physically accessible to inspectors. A purely virtual office will not be accepted for the licensed brokerage activities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High - approximately 80% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the Financial Markets Authority or the Inland Revenue Department within the first twelve months of licensed operation, given the high-risk securities brokerage classification (ISIC 6611 / NAICS 523120), retail counterparties, and the Visa/Mastercard payment rails.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), Part 2 (Incorporation), sections 12–26; Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, Part 6 (Licensing of market services), sections 396–412; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, sections 5–17
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (NZ Companies Office Form NZCN1) and Constitution (if adopted)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. The company must maintain at least one share with an issued shareholder. The Companies Office does not require escrow, capital deposit, or proof of paid-up capital at incorporation. For the offshore securities brokerage activity, the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) may impose minimum net capital or net tangible equity requirements as a condition of the market services licence, to be satisfied separately at the licensing stage.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF INTERNATIONAL COMPANY (NZ) LIMITED (the “Company”) HELD BY CIRCULAR RESOLUTION ON ________. 1. SUBSCRIPTION FOR SHARES: RESOLVED, that the subscribers to the constitution listed in the application for registration be and are hereby allotted the number of ordinary shares set opposite their respective names, credited as fully paid, and that the register of members be updated accordingly. 2. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE: RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at [Address], New Zealand, and that the Register of Directors and Register of Shareholders be maintained at such address as required by the Companies Act 1993. 3. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS: RESOLVED, that [Name] be and is hereby appointed as a director of the Company and that [Name] be and is hereby appointed as the Chief Executive Officer and [Name] be and is hereby appointed as Company Secretary, each to hold office until removed in accordance with the Companies Act 1993 and the Constitution. 4. BANK ACCOUNT AND AUTHORISED SIGNATORIES: RESOLVED, that the Company open a bank account with [Bank], New Zealand, and that the directors be authorised to execute documents and give receipts for monies paid to the Company. 5. CORPORATE GOVERNANCE AND COMPLIANCE: RESOLVED, that the Board adopt the Company’s governance charter, financial year end of 31 March, and the requirement to obtain all necessary licences, including the Financial Markets Authority licence and any anti-money laundering registration, prior to commencing regulated services. DULY RESOLVED on ________.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and Verify Availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on the NZ Companies Office register to ensure the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name. Submit an online application to reserve the name for up to 20 business days. The name must comply with the Companies Act 1993 and must not contain restricted words such as 'bank', 'trust', or 'insurance' without applicable regulatory approval. For an offshore securities brokerage, avoid using 'offshore' or 'trust' in the name unless the FMA has provided prior consent.
required_dossiers: Evidence of consent for restricted words (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to similarity or restriction, file a revised application within 5 business days with a new name or attach a letter of consent from the relevant authority (e.g., FMA for restricted financial words).

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (online portal) / Registered legal adviser or chartered accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the constitution of the company (optional if the default rules under the Companies Act 1993 are accepted; however, a tailored constitution is recommended for brokerage governance, including share transfer restrictions, director indemnity provisions, and enhanced quorum requirements). Prepare the NZCN1 application form, detailing the company name, registered office, directors, shareholders, share structure, and address for service. The constitution, if adopted, must be signed by all subscribers.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director and shareholder forms
Proof of residential address of directors/shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office queries the application, correct the identified deficiencies within 20 working days by filing an amended application or providing clarifications via the online case management interface.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Incorporation Application and Pay Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the NZCN1 application electronically through the Companies Office website, attaching all required documents. Pay the registration fee of NZD 140 (approximately USD 86.5) via secure online payment. The Companies Office will review the application for statutory compliance. The registered office must be a physical address in New Zealand, not a PO Box.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected, the Companies Office will issue a notice of rejection stating the reasons. Resubmit the corrected application within 20 working days; request priority processing if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office / New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, the Companies Office will issue a Certificate of Incorporation and automatically register the company for an NZBN. The company becomes a legal entity from the date of incorporation. Download the electronic certificate and NZBN confirmation from the Companies Office portal. The certificate is conclusive evidence of incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate or NZBN is not issued, request a reissue through the Companies Office online help desk within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File First Board Resolutions and Adopt Corporate Governance Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Board / Companies Office (for director/registered office records)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold a first board meeting or execute circular resolutions to adopt the pro forma First Board Resolution, including share subscriptions, registered office adoption, and officer appointments. Maintain minutes and resolutions in the company's statutory records. File notices of change (if any) for directors or registered office with the Companies Office within 10 working days of the change.
required_dossiers: Pro forma First Board Resolution signed
Register of Directors, Shareholders, and Ultimate Beneficial Owners
Minutes of first board meeting (if held entirely by resolution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office flags missing or inconsistent director records, file a notice of change to correct the register within 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Financial Markets Authority (FMA) Market Services Licence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) of New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a comprehensive application to the FMA for a licence to provide a market service, specifically a Derivatives Issuer Licence and/or Financial Advice Provider Licence, depending on the exact business model. The application must include a business plan, compliance programme, AML/CFT programme, fit-and-proper person declarations for directors and senior managers, and financial resource projections. The FMA will assess the application under Part 6 of the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013. If offering derivatives or CFDs to retail clients, the company must comply with the 'Issuer Obligations' and 'Financial Advice' duties.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FMA requests further information, respond to the request within the stated deadline (usually 20 days). If the licence is declined, the company may resubmit a revised application addressing the FMA's concerns or request an internal review. Administrative appeal may be made to the High Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for AML/CFT Compliance with the Department of Internal Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) – AML/CFT Group (online portal: https://aml.regulation.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: As a financial institution providing brokerage services, the company must register with the DIA as a reporting entity under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. Submit an AML/CFT registration application, including the AML/CFT compliance programme, risk assessment, and appointment of a compliance officer. The DIA will review the registration and issue an acknowledgement. This step is mandatory prior to commencing brokerage activities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DIA queries the registration, amend the compliance programme and resubmit within 15 business days. If the registration is declined, the company may apply for a review through the DIA's internal review process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with Inland Revenue for Tax Obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) New Zealand (online portal: https://www.ird.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for an IRD number and confirm tax obligations, including income tax, GST (if turnover exceeds NZD 60,000 or on voluntary registration), and employer obligations (if hiring staff). Apply for a certificate of registration for GST. The company must also provide resident withholding tax and any applicable non-resident withholding tax details. For a tax-exempt international company status (if applicable under the specific entity classification), secure the appropriate binding ruling or classification from Inland Revenue.
required_dossiers: Binding tax ruling request (if seeking exemption status)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD delays the IRD number, contact the IRD business helpdesk and email a follow-up with the Company's incorporation reference. If the GST application is rejected, revise the projection of taxable supplies and resubmit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) of New Zealand for financial services; WorkSafe New Zealand for occupational and workplace licensing; local territorial authority for premises licensing
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Market Services Licence (Derivatives Issuer Licence) under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; Financial Advice Provider Licence (if providing regulated financial advice)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based brokerage activities do not fall within the mandatory classes of activities requiring a Full EIA or Assessment of Environmental Effects (AEE) under the Environmental Protection Authority Act 2011 or the Resource Management Act 1991. However, if the brokerage establishes a physical data centre, trading floor, or warehousing facility, a project-level AEE may be required by the local territorial authority under the Resource Management Act 1991.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: New Zealand ambient air quality standards under the Resource Management (National Environmental Standards for Air Quality) Regulations 2004: office premises are not major dischargers; any backup diesel generators must comply with particulate and NOx emission thresholds. Wastewater discharges must comply with the National Environmental Standard for Sources of Human Drinking Water and the local council's trade waste bylaws. Electronic equipment waste (e-waste) must be handled in accordance with the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 and disposed of through an approved contractor. There are no VOC emission thresholds for a pure office brokerage operation; if a trading floor or data centre is housed, HVAC and cooling system refrigerants must be managed to prevent VOC leakage above the Ozone Layer Protection Act 1996 thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: WorkSafe New Zealand approval is required under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015: the company must have a documented workplace health and safety (WHS) policy, worker participation system, and hazard identification register. Fire safety clearance is to be obtained from Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) through the Fire Safety and Evacuation of Buildings Regulations 2006, which requires an evacuation scheme and annual fire drill records for any premises with more than 10 workers or a specified high-risk use. Structural load inspection and building warrant of fitness (WoF) are required from the local territorial authority under the Building Act 2004, and the premises must have appropriate Building Compliance Schedules for emergency lighting, fire alarms, and sprinklers. Operational occupational clearance for continuous sedentary office work must provide adequate ventilation, ergonomics, and egress capacity as per AS/NZS 1680 (illumination) and AS/NZS 3901 (office ergonomics).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Revenue Management Division, Ministry of Finance and Economic Management, Cook Islands (a self-governing territory in association with New Zealand); online portal: https://www.mfem.gov.ck
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Cook Islands International Company (CK IC) is automatically exempt from income tax and does not require a Tax Reference Identification Number (TRIN) unless it makes taxable supplies in the Cook Islands. If it makes such supplies, it must apply to the Revenue Management Division (RMD) using Form VAT-REG, attaching the incorporation certificate, a declaration of principal place of business, and proof of beneficial ownership. In the event the CK IC becomes a New Zealand tax resident (e.g., through central management and control moving to New Zealand), it must separately apply to Inland Revenue (IR) for an IRD number using the company registration process (IR596) and register for GST if applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The exemption is statutory and automatic under the International Companies Act 1981. No check-the-box, hybrid mismatch, or other elective regimes apply to a CK IC. If the company elects to be treated as an ordinary Cook Islands company under the Income Tax Act 1997 (by carrying on local business), it becomes taxable on worldwide income and may elect normal corporate loss-offset or group relief provisions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory e-invoicing or real-time clearing mechanism is in force. VAT-registered businesses must issue standard VAT invoices and file periodic VAT returns through the RMD portal. There is no API-based clearance or digital stamping requirement; however, the RMD may require electronic submission of returns and invoices in PDF or XML upon request.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A CK IC providing securities brokerage services to non-resident clients will zero-rate the supply for VAT purposes if the service is performed in the course of offshore business and the recipient is not resident in the Cook Islands and is not physically present in the Cook Islands when the service is rendered. The supply must not relate to any land, goods, or services physically performed in the Cook Islands. The brokerage must keep contemporaneous evidence of the client’s non-residence and the offshore nature of the transaction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / a written declaration of exportation of services (where applicable)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (only for physical deliveries, not standard for brokerage)
Inward Remittance Certificate from the Cook Islands bank confirming receipt of funds from an offshore source
Executed offshore client service agreement and trade/contract notes
Tax invoice issued to the non-resident client showing zero-rating
Certified copy of the client’s foreign tax residency certificate or passport to substantiate non-residence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The RMD may audit any zero-rated export supply. If zero-rating is applied incorrectly or without substantive documentation, the VAT shortfall is recoverable, together with statutory interest and civil penalties. Fraudulent zero-rating or deliberate misclassification attracts a penalty of up to 200% of the tax evaded, possible criminal prosecution, imprisonment, and, for an International Company, revocation of its tax-exempt status. The 180-day period is a customary internal repatriation benchmark; no specific statutory deadline applies, but unwarranted delay may trigger anti-avoidance review.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua, RBNZ) - the statutory monetary authority and banking prudential regulator for all New Zealand dollar (NZD) clearing, settlement, and foreign exchange operations. The Cook Islands does not maintain a separate central bank or independent monetary policy; the Cook Islands Dollar (CKD) is pegged at par with the NZD and the NZD is legal tender, with the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Authority (FISA) serving as the regulatory supervisor for the International Company (CK_IC) in respect of licensing, AML/CFT, and corporate administration. Accordingly, all NZD-denominated liquidity, Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) settlements, and FX intervention frameworks fall exclusively under the RBNZ mandate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand and the Cook Islands operate a fully liberalised free-float exchange-rate regime with no exchange-control legislation restricting capital or current account transactions. A non-resident-owned International Company engaged in offshore securities brokerage may freely convert NZD into any major currency, repatriate dividends, pay management fees, and remit capital without any RBNZ or FISA approval requirement. Profit remittance hurdles are therefore not of a foreign-exchange nature; the practical frictions are (i) bank counterparty de-risking of the 'High-Risk Special License' brokerage profile; (ii) AML/CFT provenance verification under the New Zealand Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 and the Cook Islands AML/CFT Act 2023; and (iii) CRS/FATCA transparency reporting. Because the entity is treated as a Tax-Exempt Zone vehicle with no New Zealand tax residence, inbound client funds and operating profits are not subject to any New Zealand exchange-control or tax-repatriation gate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Neither the Reserve Bank of New Zealand nor the Cook Islands FISA imposes any statutory surrender ratio, mandatory conversion timeline, or export-proceeds repatriation obligation. For the offshore securities brokerage activity (ISIC 6611 / NAICS 523120), client subscription monies, CFD margin flows, and Visa/Mastercard settlement proceeds are classified as financial-services and portfolio-inflow transactions rather than 'export proceeds'; they may be retained in NZD, converted to USD/EUR liquidity pools, or hedged using permitted instruments without any conversion mandate. Inward remittances are subject only to RBNZ statistical balance-of-payments reporting performed by New Zealand banks, which impose no convertibility restriction.

Segregated Client Funds Trust Account (FMC Act Part 6) and Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium feasibility. New Zealand does not operate an 'Electronic Money Institution' licensing class analogous to the EU EMD2/PSD2 regime; non-bank payment providers operate as registered banks, non-bank deposit takers, or as money remitters and payment facilitators under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008, with a prospective RBNZ payments licensing framework under consultation. Offshore digital EMIs and virtual-account providers (e.g., Wise Platform, Airwallex, and similar Treasury-as-a-Service vendors) can provide ancillary FX conversion, virtual IBAN collection, and cross-border sweep capability, but they will not accept a high-risk retail securities/CFD brokerage merchant without the IC first obtaining a New Zealand Financial Markets Authority (FMA) Derivatives Issuer licence, FSP registration, and an independent client-money audit trail. Such EMIs are therefore prohibited from holding client money; they may be used only for fringe treasury liquidity and intercompany expense disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory mandate requiring all directors to appear physically before a New Zealand bank; however, under the AML/CFT (Definitions) Regulations 2011 and RBNZ/FMA supervisory guidance, identity must be verified through an approved electronic Identity Verification Technology (IVT) connected to the Department of Internal Affairs verification framework (including RealMe) or through a physical in-person check. In practice, for a Cook Islands International Company with non-resident directors, New Zealand banks will impose a hybrid protocol: (i) at least one executive director or the appointed compliance officer must complete a live video interview with the bank's KYC team; (ii) all other directors and every ultimate beneficial owner must complete identity verification through a New Zealand consular officer, a licensed professional introducer (lawyer or accountant), or an approved IVT provider; and (iii) the bank will require a New Zealand-registered service address and a resident agent or locally incorporated compliance representative. Remote onboarding from Asia-Pacific jurisdictions is feasible using certified introducers, but the absence of any New Zealand nexus materially reduces approval probability.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity and reputational risk associated with a Cook Islands International Company (CK_IC) operating under a Tax-Exempt Zone classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Certificate of Incorporation; current Certificate of Good Standing issued by the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Authority (FISA); complete UBO schedule identifying every natural person with a direct or indirect interest; registered agent confirmation that no bearer shares are outstanding and that share registers are held in custody; CRS and FATCA self-certifications; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds dossiers for each UBO comprising audited financial statements, asset purchase deeds, tax returns, and bank provenance; board resolution approving the account-opening mandate and naming the authorised signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk financial-product classification - retail agency for equities, CFDs and derivative instruments (NAICS 523120) triggering suspicions of regulatory arbitrage or consumer-harm exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FMA Derivatives Issuer licence under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; Financial Service Provider (FSP) registration certificate; client agreement suite including risk disclosure statements and leverage limits; independent auditor's certificate on client-funds segregation (Part 6 FMC Act); capital-adequacy certificate; complaints-handling and dispute-resolution membership with an approved New Zealand scheme; audit trail of the brokerage platform connecting client orders, margin calls, and settlement reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire flows between New Zealand, low-tax territories, and higher-risk jurisdictions, creating sanctions, tax-evasion, or trade-based-money-laundering indicators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction-monitoring and sanctions-screening policy referencing UN, OFAC, EU, and NZ consolidated lists; approved counterparty jurisdiction whitelist; payment-routing topology evidencing that client funds are held only with New Zealand registered banks or licensed non-bank deposit takers; contractual prohibition on onboarding clients from FATF-monitored jurisdictions; Board AML/CFT committee minutes; external audit opinion from a licensed AML/CFT auditor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Card-acquiring exposure - Visa/Mastercard chargeback velocity, card-not-present fraud, and potential terrorism-financing via prepaid card loads.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PCI DSS Level-1 attestation of compliance; scheme-approved acquirer agreement designating the correct merchant category code; 3-D Secure authentication, velocity checks, and negative-list rules; chargeback and refund handling procedure; operational separation between card settlement float and client trading positions; quarterly fraud-loss and chargeback-ratio report; incident response and transaction-monitoring escalation protocol.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections from the parent shareholder or ultimate beneficial owners must be routed via SWIFT MT103 with the remittance information field (Field 70) referencing the specific board resolution date and class of share subscribed, for example 'INVCAP - subscription for ordinary shares per resolution dated 20XX-XX-XX'. The receiving New Zealand bank will classify the inflow for RBNZ balance-of-payments statistical reporting using the BPM6 direct-investment equity capital code and will require the corporate authorisation pack, certificate of compliance, and confirmation that the remitting bank has performed originator due diligence. Where the remitting jurisdiction applies outbound exchange controls (e.g., China ODI registration or India LRS/ODI approval), the foreign exchange approval letter must accompany the transfer and be retained in the bank's statutory records. All inbound funds must initially credit the IC's Capital Escrow Account, not the client-money trust account, and conversion to operational liquidity is permitted only after the classification is booked and the source-of-funds verification has been completed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Client withdrawals and profit remittances to non-resident beneficiaries are cleared via SWIFT MT103 messages carrying the appropriate purpose code and full sanctions screening; New Zealand domestic NZD withdrawals settle in real time through the RBNZ Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS). Visa/Mastercard settlement of retail deposits and withdrawals clears through the card acquirer's ISO 8583 interface on a T+1 settlement cycle directly into the segregated client-money account. Institution-to-institution settlements with prime brokers, liquidity providers, and FX counterparties must use SWIFT MT202 COV cover payments to satisfy Wolfsberg transparency standards for interbank cover transfers. Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600-compliant) are not a standard rail for securities brokerage commissions and are reserved for hybrid physical-commodity derivative settlements; where used, they must be issued by an AA-rated bank and matched to an underlying master agreement. All outbound client disbursements must be processed exclusively from the segregated client-money account, sequentially reconciled to the client ledger, and subjected to the withdrawal-notice and anti-fraud controls mandated by the Financial Markets Authority.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forward contracts (vanilla, up to 12-month tenors) with NZ-registered bank counterparties covering NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/JPY, and NZD/CNH exposures
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on restricted-access currencies (including CNY, KRW, INR, TWD, TRY) for margin collateral hedging through a licensed price-sourced settlement bank
Vanilla FX Options (put/call structures) and zero-cost collars designed to cap repatriation-rate volatility on operating expenses and dividend flows
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-dated matching of USD/EUR client-margin funding lines against NZD operational capital
Exchange-traded FX Futures and Options listed on CME, ASX, or SGX, cleared through a licensed Futures Commission Merchant for margining efficiency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: International Company Annual Return (ICA Form AR-1) certifying registered office, registered agent, directors, shareholders and issued/authorised share capital as at the anniversary date; fee tier assumes authorised capital not exceeding USD 100,000.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) of the Cook Islands — Office of the Registrar of International Companies, Realm of New Zealand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after each anniversary of the date of incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of USD 100; default continuing for 6 months authorises the Registrar to strike the company off the register, vest its assets with the Registrar and expose directors to fines up to USD 10,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government (Franchise) Fee payment under the International Companies (Fees) Regulations, calculated on authorised capital tiers.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before each anniversary of incorporation; no statutory grace period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge assessed for late payment; non-payment for 3 months triggers a Registrar default notice and for 6 months enables administrative strike-off and forfeiture of company property.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renewal of the FSC Offshore Securities Brokerage Licence (Special Licence classification covering retail equities, CFDs and derivative instrument dealing).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) — Licensing and Supervision Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual renewal application must be lodged at least 30 calendar days before the licence anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Continued operation without a renewed licence is a criminal offence carrying a daily penalty of USD 500; the FSC may suspend or revoke the broker licence and require an orderly transfer of segregated client assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Confirmation Return covering significant controllers, associated persons, nominee arrangements and the annual shareholding transfer log.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) — AML/CFT and Beneficial Ownership Registry, lodged through the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation is due on the incorporation anniversary; any shareholding transfer must be reported within 14 calendar days of the transfer.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil penalty up to USD 5,000 per non-filing or late filing; false beneficial ownership information is an offence punishable by up to USD 10,000 and director disqualification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AML/CFT Annual Compliance Report and independent compliance review certificate applicable to the high-risk Special Licence securities brokerage.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cook Islands Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) within the Financial Supervisory Commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the FIU-designated annual reporting date following the 30 June financial year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing is an AML/CFT Act contravention exposing the company to fines up to USD 50,000, licence suspension and appointment of a statutory manager.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general statutory audit applies to non-regulated International Companies; however, a compulsory independent audit by an FSC-approved auditor is mandatory for all licensed offshore securities brokerages classified as High-Risk Special Licence entities, regardless of revenue or asset size, with audited financial statements due to the FSC within 6 months of financial year-end.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared under IFRS as issued by the IASB on a true-and-fair-view basis for International Companies; if the brokerage is consolidated into a New Zealand parent, presentation must also align with New Zealand generally accepted accounting practice (NZ IFRS) as adopted under the Financial Markets Conduct Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The licensed registered agent must re-verify and file the beneficial ownership register with the FSC annually on the incorporation anniversary; every shareholding transfer requires pre-clearance by the registered agent and a 14-day UBO register update, with identity and source-of-funds documentation retained for at least 7 years.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800 – USD 2,500 per annum for a premium Cook Islands registered agent including registered office, Corporate Secretary, UBO register maintenance and AML/CFT compliance officer support.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 – USD 12,000 per annum for an IFRS single-entity audit of a licensed offshore securities brokerage with no subsidiaries.
